blocks.text: 16. Warnings, Errors and Troubleshooting

If the instrument encounters a problem, it enters a different state, depending on the severity of the issue. There are warnings, noncritical errors and critical errors, each having different implications and requiring different actions.
blocks.html: If the instrument encounters a problem, it enters a different state, depending on the severity of the issue. There are warnings, noncritical errors and critical errors, each having different implications and requiring different actions.

blocks.text: 16.1 Warnings

Warnings appear when unusual behaviour is detected during an otherwise successful measurement. They can indicate reduced accuracy of the measurement results or indicate impending errors. Unlike errors, warnings do not prevent the instrument from functioning, but users should pay attention to them as they can indicate sources of inaccuracies.
blocks.html: Warnings appear when unusual behaviour is detected during an otherwise successful measurement. They can indicate reduced accuracy of the measurement results or indicate impending errors. Unlike errors, warnings do not prevent the instrument from functioning, but users should pay attention to them as they can indicate sources of inaccuracies.

blocks.text: WARNING IMAGE When unusual behavior is detected, a warning is shown next to the measurement results. More information on the warning can be found by clicking on the corresponding warning entry next to the measurement results or directly in the warning log.

blocks.text: 16.2 Non-critical errors

Non-critical errors prevent a measurement from terminating successfully, but do not prevent the instrument from running another measurement afterwards. These errors do not require human intervention. Some non-critical errors are promoted to critical errors if they repeat three times.
blocks.html: Non-critical errors prevent a measurement from terminating successfully, but do not prevent the instrument from running another measurement afterwards. These errors do not require human intervention. Some non-critical errors are promoted to critical errors if they repeat three times.

blocks.text: NON-CRITICAL ERRORS The protocol stops. The cause of the error is usually fixed by repeating the analysis or waiting. • Another measurement can immediately be started. If it completes successfully, the error state is cleared. • More information on the error can be found in the error log, by clicking on the corresponding error entry.
blocks.html:
NON-CRITICAL ERRORS
The protocol stops. The cause of the error is usually fixed by repeating the analysis or waiting.
• Another measurement can immediately be started. If it completes successfully, the error state is cleared.
• More information on the error can be found in the error log, by clicking on the corresponding error entry.

blocks.text: 16.3 Critical errors

Critical errors interrupt the workflows of the instrument and require human intervention. The error source needs to be eliminated and the instrument set to running conditions again. Critical errors need to be cleared.
blocks.html: Critical errors interrupt the workflows of the instrument and require human intervention. The error source needs to be eliminated and the instrument set to running conditions again. Critical errors need to be cleared.

blocks.text: CRITICAL ERRORS IMAGE If a critical error occurs during operation, it has the following effects: • The protocol immediately stops. • The instrument goes into a critical error state, and manual intervention is needed before any new protocol can be launched. • The cause of the error must be solved by an operator. The errors can then be manually cleared from the Error log, as described in Error log and Clearing errors .
blocks.html:
CRITICAL ERRORSIMAGE
If a critical error occurs during operation, it has the following effects:
• The protocol immediately stops.
• The instrument goes into a critical error state, and manual intervention is needed before any new protocol can be launched.
• The cause of the error must be solved by an operator. The errors can then be manually cleared from the Error log, as described in Error log and Clearing errors.

blocks.text: 16.4.3 Alarm log

The Alarm log lists the alarms triggered by measurement results. It includes the instrument's own alarms (see Alarm configuration ) and, when the instrument is connected to BactoCloud, the alarms raised by BactoCloud alarm rules (see BactoCloud ). Each row shows:
blocks.html: The Alarm log lists the alarms triggered by measurement results. It includes the instrument's own alarms (see Alarm configuration) and, when the instrument is connected to BactoCloud, the alarms raised by BactoCloud alarm rules (see BactoCloud). Each row shows:

blocks.text: Date : date and time of the measurement that triggered the alarm. Name : a bell symbol and the alarm name. The bell is red for instrument alarms. For BactoCloud alarms, its color shows the severity: red for Critical, orange for Warning and blue for Info. Alarm : the alarm source, condition and threshold, for example Cartridge Remaining < 10 % .
blocks.html:
• Date: date and time of the measurement that triggered the alarm.
  • Name: a bell symbol and the alarm name. The bell is red for instrument alarms. For BactoCloud alarms, its color shows the severity: red for Critical, orange for Warning and blue for Info.
  • Alarm: the alarm source, condition and threshold, for example Cartridge Remaining < 10 %.

blocks.text: BactoCloud alarms also show a cloud symbol at the end of the row. To acknowledge a BactoCloud alarm after reviewing it, press the check button beside the cloud symbol; acknowledged alarms show a check mark instead. Acknowledge all acknowledges every unacknowledged BactoCloud alarm in the list and is only available while at least one remains. Acknowledgement is recorded in BactoCloud. It documents the review but does not resolve the cause of the alarm.

blocks.text: Audit trail lists relevant operations and setting changes made by users or by the instrument. Each entry shows the Date , the User and the Event and, where they apply, the changed Parameter with its Old value and New value . The audit trail is also included when exporting all data to a USB drive and can be viewed in the web user interface.

blocks.text: 16.4.5 Changing the displayed time span
The following procedure applies to the Error log , Warning log , Alarm log and Audit trail .
blocks.html: The following procedure applies to the Error log, Warning log, Alarm log and Audit trail.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Open the log and press the time span button next to Displayed time span: . The Define time span screen opens. 2. Tap the field under Start date and select the first day in the calendar. Tap the time field below it and set the hour and minute. Set End date and its time in the same way. The end cannot be earlier than the start. 3. Press OK . The log lists only the entries within the selected period.

blocks.text: 16.5 Clearing errors

Critical errors must be cleared manually. Make sure to first solve the origin of the problem, then manually clear the error with the steps below. Please note that the procedure below does not automatically solve the root cause of the error.
blocks.html: Critical errors must be cleared manually. Make sure to first solve the origin of the problem, then manually clear the error with the steps below. Please note that the procedure below does not automatically solve the root cause of the error.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 2. Press Logs , then Error log . 3. Make sure you have resolved the problem leading to the displayed error(s). Then press Clear errors . The button is available to Basic, Advanced and Admin users while no protocol is running. 4. A C02 – Errors cleared manually event is added at the top of the log, and the symbols of the earlier errors turn grey. The instrument is ready to analyze again.

blocks.text: 16.6 Automatic self-check
The automatic self-check tool checks that each component of the BactoSense is functioning correctly and identifies those that are not. It can be used to identify problems with the instrument.
blocks.html: The automatic self-check tool checks that each component of the BactoSense is functioning correctly and identifies those that are not. It can be used to identify problems with the instrument.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. 3. Press the Self-check button. 4. Additional information Press the Rerun button. Once execution has terminated, the instrument shows a list of all tests, with a green PASS or red FAIL indicator. Some tests may be skipped: if the system cannot communicate with the cartridge, all the tests that require cartridge communication are skipped.

blocks.text: 16.7 Operation at low temperature

The instrument must be operated within a specific temperature range to prevent damage and ensure reliable and reproducible measurement results (see Technical data ). At very low and very high ambient temperatures (below 5 °C (41 °F) or above 30 °C (86 °F)), protocols are not executed. At low ambient temperatures, the instrument automatically warms up prior to a measurement to reach the required temperature. During this heating process, the instrument status shows “Heating...”. If the target temperature cannot be reached after several hours, the protocol exits with an error (table 16-2, E42).

blocks.text: Allow time for heating Measurements can be delayed if extensive heating is necessary. To avoid this, keep the instrument temperature above 10 °C (50 °F).
blocks.html:
ALLOW TIME FOR HEATING

Measurements can be delayed if extensive heating is necessary. To avoid this, keep the instrument temperature above 10 °C (50 °F).
